{"chunk_id":"5e56ce","wall_time_seconds":0.000007125,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":2558,"output":"# Scoping

A prototype answers one unresolved behavior or visual question that a person can experience. Define the decision, audience, success signal, and explicit non-goals before building. Unattended pipeline work, production write-back, and prototypes without a human experience remain blocked.

## Resolve the question

Use the current conversation and any supplied brainstorm or plan. An empty invocation may use an already stated question; disclose meaningful inferences from messy history and ask only for missing information. A repo run concerns that product unless the user says otherwise. Inspect only the page, component, or flow the question touches, its current behavior, paths, and constraints; do not scan the whole tree or request an architecture summary. Perform the bounded read inline unless the current user or authorized caller explicitly requested delegation.

Before building, know the product surface, the decision, and hard constraints. Do not ask the user to invent the answer in chat. Start with the uncertainty most expensive to get wrong, combining parts when their interaction is the question. Do not rebuild a visual question the user already settled against an adequate artifact.

## Narrow or wide

- **Narrow:** compare two or three close variants of a specific control, placement, or transition on one suitable surface; do not invent unrelated mechanisms.
- **Wide:** explore three to five distinct mechanisms within the named product question, describing what the user would see or do. This is not product discovery. Let the user choose avenues or build a comparable subset, then converge against the artifacts. Do not build one idea as the presumed answer.

Resolve unclear width from context, asking once when the distinction materially changes the build. Size to the uncertainty, not to the cheapest remaining question. A coupled flow may require a larger prototype than an isolated placement decision; fidelity is a separate choice owned by the build reference.

## Before and between builds

Before a costly preview, state what you will try, why, how it is split, and any consequential inference. Honor an existing explicit go-ahead for that scope; ask only when it is missing or the proposed effects exceed it. The user can redirect the question. Do not treat silence as approval or the agent's visual judgment as the user's decision.

After a human decision, reread the capsule and reassess remaining questions. The choice may settle another question, make it irrelevant, or reveal a new one. Explain meaningful changes before the next build. If the product goal itself changes, return the learning to its owner instead of continuing an obsolete question.
# Build

Build in a private throwaway root with loopback preview and a decision log. Keep generated assets and production source separate. Record the exact run command, preview URL, cleanup receipt, and what the human observed before making a recommendation.

## Fidelity and medium

Throwaway means unmaintained and unshipped, not necessarily low fidelity. Make a state or flow question rich enough to drive, a visual direction finished enough to judge, and an isolated placement only as detailed as needed. Do not add production abstractions or hardening beyond runnable, and persist state only when persistence is the question. Fidelity can differ among avenues.

Use the web by default. Honor a user-named technology or a tested dimension that cannot be represented honestly in a browser; state that choice before building. If the named technology cannot express the dimension either, report the limitation. Within the preview page, use available image generation when appropriate; markup is a valid fallback only when it honestly carries the dimension. A photographic or painterly question cannot be replaced by a markup sketch. Do not introduce a second display mechanism beside the preview; a non-web medium uses its own suitable display.

## Build and compare

Recreate only what the question needs from the current product. Do not stand up the full app unless the question concerns the whole-product experience. This local Skill preserves isolated artifacts and does not edit production source for overlays; when isolated reproduction cannot answer a density/chrome question, report that limitation to the owning workflow instead of silently expanding mutation scope.

Put comparable options on one surface unless that distorts the dimension. Scroll and transition questions need full-size interactive runs, with a static comparison surface if useful. Show the relevant state after a variant or user-facing action changes. Use one child directory per question beneath the single run directory selected by the preview reference. Never delete a kept prototype merely because its code is throwaway.

## Decision capsule

Only after a human actually settles a choice, update `decisions.md` with the question, what was built, run and question paths, the winner and reason, rejected options, requested adjustments, adjustments not yet in the artifact, and open questions. Preserve the winner and agreed adjustments in the prototype where feasible. Do not ask again before recording an already settled decision, and do not invent a winner from a passing test. The capsule is continuity for brainstorm or planning, not an implementation plan; multiple unresolved choices remain explicitly unresolved.
# Preview

Resolve one private run root, then reuse its canonical absolute path for every server operation. Prefer the ignored in-repo `.context/compound-engineering/ce-prototype` root. When that root is unsafe, not ignored, declined, or outside a Git repository, use a Node helper based on `os.tmpdir()` so Windows, macOS, and Linux use their native private temporary root.

Settle durability before claiming the directory. From the resolved repo root, probe `git -C <repo-root> check-ignore -q .context/compound-engineering/`; the trailing slash checks the directory. If the user wants repo-local retention and this path is not ignored, propose the single repo-root `.gitignore` entry and append it only within explicit authorization, preserving existing contents. If they requested no repo copy, skip that offer and use temporary storage. Resolve these facts once, then claim the root; never create a preliminary directory and re-resolve into a suffixed sibling.

Before using the example below, prove `preferredRootIsIgnoredAndSafe` by inspecting every path segment from the canonical repo root, rejecting symlinks, non-directories, and directories not owned by the current user where ownership is supported. An unsafe preferred path falls back to temporary storage; it is not repaired with chmod. The example's fallback uses exclusive `mkdtempSync` directly under the OS temporary root rather than following a shared fixed directory.

```javascript
const fs = require('node:fs');
const os = require('node:os');
const path = require('node:path');

const preferredRoot = path.join(repoRoot, '.context', 'compound-engineering', 'ce-prototype');
if (preferredRootIsIgnoredAndSafe) {
  fs.mkdirSync(preferredRoot, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
}
const prefix = preferredRootIsIgnoredAndSafe
  ? path.join(fs.realpathSync(preferredRoot), 'run-')
  : path.join(fs.realpathSync(os.tmpdir()), 'spec-first-ce-prototype-');
const runDir = fs.mkdtempSync(prefix);
process.stdout.write(`${fs.realpathSync(runDir)}\n`);
```

The preview server must receive the printed `RUN_DIR` through the `--root` argument. Re-check that the directory is owned by the current user and is not a symlink before each start, status, or stop call.

Temporary storage offers only best-effort survival. Report that limitation and preserve kept artifacts; do not promise a lifetime or delete the directory during ordinary preview cleanup.

After changing HTML or same-origin assets, explicitly refresh the same preview URL and inspect the changed state before asking for a decision. The server sends `Cache-Control: no-store`; it does not inject live reload. `/version` identifies the newest screen name, not a digest of same-name edits, so do not use that response as proof the browser displays current bytes. Keep this manual refresh path rather than adding a polling service that prolongs an unattended preview's lifetime.

Start with the default `127.0.0.1` binding or explicit `--host ::1`; every other host is rejected. The server emits a CSP that permits only same-origin assets/connections plus inline prototype code, keeps an owner-private instance token out of user output, and proves lifecycle ownership through a token-bound loopback identity endpoint. Stop asks the identified server to close itself; it never sends a signal directly to a PID. A blocked stop is a limitation requiring manual owner inspection, not permission to send a broader signal.
# Craft floor

Apply only what the visual question puts in play. The render must be specific to the product and question, not a generic template or a palette-only variation. Distinct avenues differ by organizing principle, not by superficial spacing or color swaps; the wide-run rule lives in `references/scoping.md`.

For text that is part of the judgment, preserve readable contrast: body text at least 4.5:1 and large text at least 3:1. Check the actual rendered state at the target viewport before recording a decision.

When the question depends on controls or transitions, include usable focus, visible loading/empty/error states and honest action feedback. Use representative content density and copy so overflow, truncation and hierarchy can be judged. Inspect relevant viewport/state pairs; a screenshot of the default state does not validate an interaction. Apply only the parts needed to answer the question, and record limitations when an isolated page cannot reproduce the production context.
# Write-back

Only write back after a human has experienced the prototype and selected a direction. Preserve the existing Product Contract or related plan as the owning artifact; add the decision and prototype evidence without copying throwaway implementation code. If no choice was made, keep the run as an unresolved input and recommend returning to `spec-brainstorm` or `spec-plan`.
"}
